Samayam.com published an article on May 26, 2021, titled "Can lemon and hot water kill coronavirus experts bust these popular myths." The article states that the idea of lemon and hot water killing the coronavirus is a misconception and completely false. It mentions that videos and myths about lemon and hot water circulating on social media are abundant, but there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that lemon drops in the nose can kill the coronavirus. [1]

AFP Fact Check published an article on March 12, 2020, titled "False claims that drinking water with lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online." The article refutes the claim that drinking warm water with lemon protects against the novel coronavirus, stating that experts found no proof of its effectiveness in preventing the disease. [2]

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine published information on April 22, 2020, stating that the acid in lemon juice will not kill coronaviruses in the body and consuming acidic drinks like lemon juice has no effect on coronavirus infections. [3] They further clarify that lemon juice will not destroy viruses or stop their replication, and there is no evidence that lemons or vitamin C supplements can "boost" the immune system to protect against infections. [3]

VOANews.com published an article on May 18, 2021, titled "The Infodemic: Lemon Juice Won't Cure COVID-19." This article states that the claim that a few drops of lemon juice in the nose will cure COVID-19 is false. [4]

FactCheck.org published an article on April 2, 2020, titled "Lemon Juice Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel, or Anywhere Else." The article debunks the baseless claim that a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice will "eliminate" the novel coronavirus. [5] An infectious diseases physician confirmed that there is no data to show that lemon juice or hot tea would kill a virus. [5]

A study published by NIH on June 10, 2022, titled "Association of natural products use with COVID-19 severity and hospitalization," found that regular consumption of lemon and citrus fruits before infection was associated with a substantial reduction in COVID-19 severity and a significant decrease in the frequency of COVID-19-induced hospitalization. [6] However, this study focuses on the association of natural product *consumption* with severity and hospitalization, not on lemon juice *destroying* the virus. [6]
